source.basis: Operator facility page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
Stack Infrastructure's POR03 campus in Hillsboro, Oregon occupies 182,000 square feet of technical space. The operator has not published a megawatt figure for this facility, so no IT load, critical power, or rack capacity can be derived from the spec page. Without a power number, any translation into racks or accelerators would require assuming both a density and a total load, compounding the uncertainty to the point where the result would be uninformative.

Oregon context sharpens what that omission means. This site has mapped 133 data center facilities in the state, of which only 6 have published a megawatt figure, together totaling 182 MW of disclosed capacity. POR03 is not among those six. The campus would rank seventh by published megawatts if a figure were available, but because none is, it sits outside the ranked set entirely. The 182,000 square feet of technical space is the only quantitative signal the operator has chosen to make public.

For a reader evaluating AI relevance, technical square footage alone is a weak signal. A building of that size could support anything from low-density colocation to high-density GPU clusters depending on power infrastructure, cooling architecture, and floor loading, none of which Stack Infrastructure has published for POR03. Until a critical power figure appears on the spec page, this campus cannot be placed confidently on the compute-capacity map that matters for AI workloads.
